input.title: Small can be smart-and smooth: The Cayman Islands' relations abroad and effects at home
input.abstract: The Cayman Islands were among the first micro-states to establish a thriving offshore financial services industry by exploiting their historical status as a tax-free jurisdiction. This was threatened when concern about the laundering of the proceeds of drug-trafficking induced the United States to challenge bank secrecy laws in the Caymans and other financial centres. This article demonstrates how decision-makers in the islands shrewdly secured the assistance of their protecting power, Britain, to gain leverage in negotiations with the United States, how they developed a negotiating brief and thereby created model arrangements that permit the exchange of certain financial information, while protecting the financial security of the legitimate patrons of their banks. © 1998 John Wiley & Sons, Ltd.

output.reasoning: O artigo não atende aos critérios básicos de busca por palavras-chave do protocolo (métodos computacionais, lavagem de dinheiro ou crime organizado) nos campos de título, resumo ou palavras-chave dos autores.
